title: Copilot Studio: PPAC Reporting API for daily usage data
summary: The roadmap facts and existing reporting and cost-control instructions are supported. The briefing appropriately leaves the new API's entitlement and rollout behaviour open; its background licensing paragraph should acknowledge the alternative access routes in Microsoft's licensing overview.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Existing environment, agent and user consumption reports are available in Power Platform admin center through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Download report.
claims.quote:
On the navigation pane, select Licensing.
In the Licensing pane, under Products, select Copilot Studio.
Select the Summary tab.
Select Download report.
Select the download type you need: environment, agent, or user.

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The existing tenant licensing report generation operation is POST https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/licensing/reports/{ReportName}?api-version=2024-10-01.
claims.quote:
Starts generating a Copilot Studio licensing report for your tenant over the requested date range.
POST https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/licensing/reports/{ReportName}?api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: The licensing report request body has a startDate property.
claims.quote: startDate | True | string (date) | The inclusive UTC start date of the report range.

claims.claim: The licensing report request body has an endDate property.
claims.quote: endDate | True | string (date) | The inclusive UTC end date of the report range. Must be on or after the start date.

claims.claim: The licensing report request body has a granularity property.
claims.quote: granularity | | CopilotStudioLicensingReportGranularity | The granularity of a licensing report. Daily returns one row per day in the date range, and Summary returns a single summarized row for the whole range.

claims.quote: Requires the Global, Dynamics 365, or Power Platform administrator role.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Existing per-agent monthly consumption limits are managed in Power Platform admin center through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents.
claims.quote:
On the navigation pane, select Licensing.
In the Licensing pane, under Products, select Copilot Studio.
On the Summary tab, select Manage Agents.
You can set a monthly limit for any agent directly from this page.

claims.claim: An agent's monthly-limit hard stop automatically turns the agent off when it reaches the defined limit.
claims.quote: Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.

claims.claim: Monthly limits are not applied instantly and an agent can continue responding for some time after reaching its limit.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit does not stop the agent flows it calls.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited licensing page says creating and managing Copilot Studio agents requires a Copilot Studio User License for each user.
claims.quote:
To create and manage agents with Copilot Studio, you need:
A license for each user, also known as a per user license (or Copilot Studio User License as referred to on the Microsoft 365 admin center).
claims.fix: Qualify the background licensing statement in licensing.notes and Cost and licensing: 'The cited page lists a Copilot Studio User License per author and a tenant licence for standard-harness agent authoring. The licensing overview also lists Copilot Studio authors access, a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence or a trial licence as access routes.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing, whose 'Get started in Copilot Studio' section lists those alternatives. Keep the new reporting API's own entitlement open.

claims.claim: The existing admin centre user report documents user-level consumption for standard-harness agents.
claims.quote: The reports show consumption by environment and agent. For agents powered by the standard harness, the user report also shows consumption by user.

claims.claim: The existing user report can show unauthenticated-session usage under an all-zero user ID without a user name.
claims.quote: In the user report, usage from sessions where the user didn't sign in, for example on an agent that doesn't require authentication, can appear under the user ID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 with no user name.
